findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with non-numeric second field causes panic instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: Use ? or map_err to propagate ParseError; return Result<Vec<Record>, E> from the function

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width-reducing cast from u32 to u16; values > 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: out-of-range parsed values wrap around silently, producing invalid domain data
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed) and propagate the error via ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec by index without bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: empty or whitespace-only lines produce an empty parts Vec; indexing panics at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case; skip or error on malformed lines

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the Vec by index without bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one comma-delimited field (missing value) panic at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly two fields and handle the missing-second-field case

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec for a two-field CSV record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and iteration; HOLzman rule mandates split_once for first-delimiter extraction
findings.fix: Replace with line.split_once(',') and handle the (name, value) tuple directly

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println), and parsing logic in one function
findings.failure_mode: impossible to unit-test parsing without mocking filesystem; println side effect cannot be suppressed in tests; violates pure core / imperative shell boundary
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_record: &str -> Result<Record, ParseError> for the core; keep the shell function for fs::read_to_string and println at the boundary

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect inside a data-parsing pipeline
findings.failure_mode: logging leaks into the pure calculation layer; cannot be tested or suppressed; breaks deterministic core
findings.fix: Remove println from the pure function; if logging is needed, return a log event alongside the record or handle it in the shell layer

findings.problem: Record has public fields (pub name: String, pub value: u16) allowing construction of invalid state outside the module
findings.failure_mode: callers can create Record with empty name or out-of-range value without going through validation
findings.fix: Make fields private and provide a constructor or builder that enforces invariants, or use newtypes for name (e.g., struct Name(String)) with validation

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> instead of Result<Vec<Record>, E>, swallowing all per-line parse failures
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed line would panic (via unwrap) rather than failing the entire load with a typed error describing which line and why
findings.fix: Change signature to load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError> where SessionLoadError wraps IoError and ParseError

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions performance (CSV parsing throughput)
no profiler data to confirm this hot path or any other is actually hot
no allocation analysis (no measured per-record allocation budget)
no second-ring review (black-hat review, contract verification, or proof artifacts absent)
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy not run)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 10 blocker-level Holzman violations spanning unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, split misuse, functional core violation, and missing error propagation. Every violation is independently gradable with concrete failure modes. The code must be fully rewritten to return Result types, use split_once, eliminate unwrap/as, separate pure parsing from I/O/shell, and add invariant enforcement before any delivery gate.
